description: A well-designed additive migration: workspace_id cascades correctly, created_by uses ON DELETE RESTRICT to preserve keys/audit trail if the creating user is removed, every required column is NOT NULL, the (workspace_id, name) uniqueness is correctly tenant-scoped rather than global, and key_hash has its own necessary global-uniqueness index. Zero findings expected.
explanation: A direct contrast to this benchmark's buggy fixtures, using the SAME shapes deliberately: `workspace_id ... on delete cascade` (correct here, unlike the audit-log fixture's actor_id), `created_by ... on delete restrict` (correct — the opposite bug from the audit-log fixture, preserving history when a user is removed), a per-tenant `unique (workspace_id, name)` (correct — a good reviewer must not demand this be a bare, globally-unique `name`, which would incorrectly block two different workspaces from both naming a key 'ci-deploy'), and a separate, genuinely-global-scope unique index on key_hash (correct, since a hash must be a reliable global lookup key). A reviewer that over-generalizes from the buggy fixtures — 'cascade is always wrong' or 'uniqueness should always be as broad as possible' — will fail this fixture.
